gate.how: node --experimental-strip-types via registerHooks, importing gateSense directly; all 58 rows passed through it
gate.result: 58/58 ok on the first pass, no repair round
gate.pre_write_check: Rule A'1: every candidate content word was grep-checked against allowed-words BEFORE drafting, in four batches. That check rejected in advance: airport, glove, careless, polite, rude, cruel, brave, clever, foolish, fake, bake, boil, exit, hidden, forbid, dictionary, towel, soap, website, asleep, monkey, steam, centre, internet, and every spelled-out numeral above one. Those words never entered a draft sentence, which is why the gate saw zero level drift.
gate.post_gate_check: Two item stems were rewritten AFTER the gate passed them, for a defect the gate cannot see: the stem forced a plural while the answer key is the singular headword ('lasted several ____' -> hours; 'has many ____ of good writing' -> examples). Gate re-run clean after the rewrite.

spot_check.note: batch is smaller than 80, so every sense is marked spot_check=true

headword_source.change_from_previous_runs: TD-17 is PARTLY STALE: the canonical domain answered this run. Batches 08-07..08-11 used an unverified GitHub mirror because the origin was unreachable then. This batch takes its headwords and their frequency order from the canonical file, columns 'Lemma,SFI Rank,SFI,Adjusted Frequency per Million (U)'; only the Lemma column was used.
headword_source.caveat: The canonical file reports 2,800 data rows, not the documented 2,809. The discrepancy is UNRESOLVED and is a finding for the Critic (see plan/03-for-roy.md). It does not affect ranks 195-260, which are all high-frequency core English.
headword_source.allowed_words_provenance_gap: allowed-words-2026-08-07.txt is still derived from the GitHub mirror (2,818 lemmas) and was NOT rebuilt this run, so the level check still rests on the mirror. Rebuilding it from the canonical list belongs to T-042/T-043, not to a content tick.

selection_rule: ascending NGSL SFI rank from the canonical stats file, skipping any headword that already has a row in data/generated/. The five earlier batches covered 225 headwords; the 45 most frequent still-uncovered headwords sit at ranks 195-260.
sense_policy: D-021 - one row per sense. 12 of the 45 headwords carry more than one sense (state, move, order x3, issue, second, love, offer, lead, face, room, form, head), so 45 headwords produced 58 rows.
distractor_policy: D-023 plus lessons 6 and 7 of plan/80-content-lessons.md: every batch row is 2 semantic + 1 orthographic + 1 unrelated, zero near_synonym, zero antonyms, and each of the 232 distractors was substituted into all three of its own stems before it was written.
